answer: To keep a flood of fake identities from capturing votes, every new agent posts a slashable onyx collateral at one shared registration inlet before it can attest or earn. After the bond locks, the network runs a short gale of unsynchronized challenges: established peers demand distinct work traces and key-origin proofs on staggered clocks. Clones fail the timing and reuse patterns, the cluster is merged, and the bond is burned. Multiplying accounts then multiplies capital at risk, so a sybil swarm costs more than it can extract.
